text:
Priya S.: Heads up — Citrine asked for a short-but-realistic perf validation next week. Scope: sustain 200 qps steady, p50 < 75ms, p99 < 300ms. Requirement #2: multi-region failover (us-west-2 -> eu-west-1) with failover completion < 60s. Also validate microbursts: 1k qps for 20s every 15m. They want a one-page results summary + answers for security questionnaire (logs/PII, retention). Can eng run this and give a rough pricing delta for Dedicated 6xA10G vs hybrid hosted + bursts?

Marco: I can own the run. Quick clarifying Qs: which model and token sizes? Also do they care about cold-starts vs warm-only? That affects warm-cache strategy.

Priya S.: Model: redwood/open-chat-7b-quant. Typical prompt ~120 tokens, generation ~80 tokens. They care about both cold-start and warm failover (so we'll run both scenarios).

Lena: Notes from infra POV: for that mix, steady 200 qps will use batching nicely on A10G quant path. For failover target (<60s) we need warm standby in eu-west-1 (model already prefetched) otherwise cold image pull + model init will blow the window. Plan: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (6xA10G) + warm burst nodes in eu-west-1 (2xA10G) for the failover experiment.

Marco: Draft runbook (short):
- Provision: us-west-2 cluster (6xA10G), eu-west-1 warm standby (2xA10G), loadgens in both regions (m5.4xlarge).
- Warm: run prefix-warm for 15m to populate KV caches and JIT paths.
- Steady: 200 qps for 90m to capture stable distribution.
- Burst injection: schedule 1k qps for 20s every 15m for 6 cycles.
- Failover: run normal steady in us-west then cut route and shift 100% traffic to eu-west; measure time to p50/p99 recovery and token drop rate.

Load command (internal harness; example):
```
./benchctl --endpoint https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  --payload citrine_template.json --qps 100 --clients 10 --duration 90m
# bursts we spawn short jobs: --qps 1000 --duration 20s
```
(we orchestrate bursts so they look like real client patterns).

Marco: Measurement targets: p50/p90/p99, gpu_util, queue_len, tokens/sec, rejected/timeout counts, and estimated cost-per-1M-tokens. We'll also capture traces around the failover event.

SecurityBot: Questionnaire snippet you can paste: "Request payloads are redacted at the edge by default; logs retain anonymized request IDs, route metadata, and non-user metadata (latency, model ID). Customers requiring full TEA-level separation can opt for Private deployment with customer-controlled KMS and dedicated audit log sinks. Retention defaults: 30 days for perf/ops metrics, 7 days for request traces; configurable via enterprise contract."

Priya S.: Pricing ask: ballpark numbers so I can push back in commercial thread. Can someone give a quick delta (very rough) between Dedicated 6xA10G monthly vs hosted + bursts approach?

Lena: Rough ballpark (pre-contract): Dedicated 6xA10G commit ~ "$140k/mo" (includes reserved infra + platform fee). Hybrid (smaller commit 3xA10G + hosted bursts to cover peaks) tends to add ~20-30% premium on peak hours due to burst pricing and cross-region egress; depends on burst cadence. I'll annotate exact $ after we measure tokens/sec/GPU in the steady run.

Marco: Timeline: I'll run a smoke today to validate tooling, then schedule the full run Tue 01:00-08:00 UTC (low traffic). I'll push raw artifacts + perf dashboard to this thread after the run. Draft writeup (1-pager + spreadsheet) by Tue EOD.

OpsBot: ✅ clusters provisioned: citrine-usw2-6gpu, citrine-euw1-2gpu, loadgen-nodes up. Model image: redwood/open-chat-7b-quant:v3. Warm scripts staged.

Lena: Operational tips during run: 1) start prefix-warm script at t-20m; 2) monitor queue_len and if avg queue_len > 150 during bursts, add one extra GPU or enable more aggressive batching; 3) for failover, pre-warm eu-west traffic shaping so the drop isn't all-or-nothing.

Priya S.: Perfect. Please include a short section in the writeup called "Commercial implications" that maps observed effective tokens/sec per GPU to monthly projected spend under both commit and hybrid models. I'll feed that into the deal doc.

Marco: Will do. Attaching link to perf dashboard once run completes. cc @Lena @SecurityBot for the writeup checklist. :white_check_mark:
